summary:
Identifying Earth Locations that Analog potential Base and Landing locations on terrestrial bodies.

We developed a custom web app called ExoMetric to use to compare Earth locations to lunar and Martian locations. By selecting a location on either the Earth, Moon or Mars, this web app allows you to compare various factors across the other bodies using open source NASA and other data. The webapp also allows you to see more information about how the data was gathered and how it might affect the mission viability. There is a number of toggles available to influence how strongly you want to consider each individual parameter, which would vary based on the nature of the mission, be it an unmanned or manned mission.
details:
Every rover and habitat sent to the Moon or Mars is tested on Earth first, in deserts, lava fields and polar ice. But which Earth site is the right stand-in for a particular crater or plain? Today that choice relies on expert judgment and a handful of famous analogs. We built ExoMetric to make it measurable.

ExoMetric is a web app for the classification, comparison and visualization of Earth analogs for potential landing and base locations on the Moon and Mars. It helps mission teams find the right Earth sites for practical testing. Students and hobbyists are also easily able to learn from our intuitive, visual website.

By utilizing over a dozen open databases from NASA and other space agencies, ExoMetric is able to pinpoint a location on both the moon and mars that is the most similar to earth by various climate and terrain metrics. By weighing the importance of a variety of factors including temperature, solar energy, terrain similarities, and soil composition with these sliders, mission planners are able to tailor the tool to the specific needs of each mission, whether a probe is being landed, or a permanent base is being established.

On the left side of the webapp, you are able to select from a large database of known locations on either terrestrial body and correlate them back to the best matching location on earth. This is useful in order to assist in performing the rigorous mechanical and field testing NASA needs to undergo in order to test their rovers and bases before sending them into space. If specific factors are not relevant for the mission, they can be omitted from the data and the strongest location can be located.

It is also possible to visualize specific weather, temperature and terrain features on the terrestrial bodies with the inclusion of heatmaps, showing the similarities over an area based on the open source NASA data.

To further visualize this data for both researchers, hobbyists, and students alike, ExoMetric also displays a variety this open source NASA data in an easily digestible way, to showcase how one metric can alter the best matching location it finds. Students can also better understand why certain patterns emerge on terrestrial bodies and why they are used when finding analogs here on earth.

Some datasets, like soil composition and local wind speed, are still sparse for the Moon and Mars. As new data arrives, or using ground stations to feed in local measurements, the matches get sharper.

ExoMetric identifies the best analogs to lunar and Martian landing locations, anywhere on earth.
